title: Prompt sanitization & trust-boundary sketch
content:
Context / goal:
- Quick personal sketch for how client-side + edge sanitization could sit relative to the Redwood serving runtime. Not a final design, more of a set of options and tradeoffs to surface in sync with SecOps and Edge client teams.

Motivation:
- Customers want control over PII leakage, hallucination surface, and untrusted prompt content coming from client devices (mobile/embedded).
- Need a pattern that lets us enforce policy without killing UX (latency, helpful autocompletion).

Assumptions:
- We control the runtime and can inject middleware at the edge (reverse proxy) and at the server side.
- Some customers will run Redwood Private (on-prem) and may want the same primitives.
- Threats: accidental PII in user prompts, malicious prompts that try to exfiltrate tokens/credentials, prompt injection from clipboard/shared state.

Design goals (ranked):
1) Low-latency default path (no extra RTT beyond typical hosted).
2) Configurable policy at customer level (allow deny, redact, flag-only).
3) Auditable actions (who/when/what changed).
4) Composable: support client hints (like 'explicit_consent: true') and server overrides.

High-level options explored:
A. Pure client-side: JS/SDK sanitization hooks\  - Pros: earliest, reduces tokens sent to Redwood, better privacy for client-only heuristics\  - Cons: trust problem (client can be bypassed), inconsistent behavior across SDKs/versions\B. Edge/Proxy filter (recommended default for hosted):\  - Pros: enforceable by us, central policy, can use ML classifiers at scale\  - Cons: risk of additional latency, needs capacity and monitoring\C. Server-side post-hoc detection + feedback loop:\  - Pros: minimal latency impact on request path if async, good for detection and auditing\  - Cons: reactive (too late to stop leakage)\D. Hybrid: client hints + edge enforcement + async server audits (favored)\  - Flow: client applies best-effort masking, edge applies hard rules (deny/redact), server audits and issues regressions/alerts\\nASCII diagram (very rough):

  [Client SDK] --(1)--> [Edge Filter / Proxy] --(2)--> [Runtime Router] --(3)--> [Model Pod]
      |                 |                      |
      |(a) client-hints   |(b) policy decision   |(c) audit events (async)
      v                 v                      v
  (optional) local UI  (policy engine)      (audit pipeline)

Example policy shape (sketch - JSON-ish, prefer compact):
  policy_id: 'cust-1234-prompt-policy-v1'
  rules: [
    { id: 'redact-ssn', match: 'regex', pattern: "\\d{3}-\\d{2}-\\d{4}", action: 'redact', priority: 100 },
    { id: 'deny-credit-card', match: 'keyword', pattern: ['credit card', 'cc number'], action: 'deny', priority: 200 },
    { id: 'flag-personal-email', match: 'regex', pattern: "[a-z0-9._%+-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+\\.[a-z]{2,}", action: 'flag', priority: 50 }
  ]
  enforcement_mode: 'edge-strong'  # options: edge-strong | edge-signal-only | server-audit-only
  client_hints: ['explicit_consent', 'redaction_preference']

Edge filter behavior (notes):
- On match action: 'redact' => substitute with metadata token '<REDACTED:type>' and continue
- action: 'deny' => return 403 with structured error payload and telemetry id
- action: 'flag' => allow but add header 'X-Redwood-Flag: <rule-id>' and emit audit event

Performance considerations:
- Regex-heavy policy sets need optimized path: compile rules to deterministic automata, prefer Aho-Corasick for keywords, RE2 for safe regex engines.
- For expensive ML checks (PII classifier), run on CPU pool with async path + fallback. Inline fast models (quantized small transformer) could run on the edge for 95th percentile latency constraints.

API surface sketches:
1) GET /v1/policies/{customer} -> returns effective policy meta (etag, enforcement_mode, summary)
2) POST /v1/policies/{customer}/validate -> dry-run a prompt through policy engine, returns actions+positions
3) POST /v1/sanitize -> (internal/edge-only) body: { prompt: '...', customer: 'cust-1234', client_hints: {...} } -> returns { prompt: '...', redaction_map: [...], flags: [...] }

SDK hint model (client):
- RedwoodSDK.sanitize(prompt, options) -> returns { sanitized_prompt, redaction_map } // optional helper
- RedwoodSDK.send({ prompt, client_hints }) // normal send, edge will enforce

Telemetry / auditing:
- Every enforcement decision emits audit event with: request_id, policy_id, rule_id, action, snippet_hash (for dedupe), user_id (if available), timestamp
- Audit retention policy tied to customer plan; default 90d, enterprise can extend

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to represent 'intent' vs 'literal PII'? E.g., 'What is the SSN format?' vs actual SSN. Need context-aware classifier.
- UX for redaction: show inline redaction vs ask user for consent? Mobile UX constraints.
- Multi-tenant sharing of classifier models: should we provide a shared PII model or let customers supply custom matchers?
- How to support offline client flows where sanitization must be performed without contacting edge? Bundle local patterns or allow offline config sync?

Migration plan (quick):
1) MVP: add 'flag' mode on edge for small rule set (SSN, CC, email) -> no latency/regression risk
2) Phase 2: add 'redact' substitution + SDK helpers to surface redactions in UI
3) Phase 3: add ML classifier + async audit pipeline + admin UI for policies

Notes for next sync with SecOps (agenda):
- Show small demo of POST /v1/policies/{cust}/validate with sample prompts
- Perf targets for edge filter: p95 < 5ms for regex-only, p95 < 25ms for small model-run
- Data retention / GDPR concerns for audit logs

Quick sketches / helper commands (local dev):
- run-local-filter: docker compose up filter --env POLICY_FILE=./examples/test-policy.json
- validate-sample: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/policies/test/validate -d '{\'prompt\':\'send my ssn 123-45-6789\'}'

References / related tickets:
- ENG-4321 (PII policy engine proto)
- SEC-110 (audit retention requirements)
- GH PR: runtime/pull/987 (edge filter initial impl)

Random thoughts (brain dump):
- Could use a tokenized redaction approach: keep a reversible redaction token for enterprise on-prem customers (KMS-wrapped) so they can decrypt server-side for debugging with appropriate audit logs.
- Provide an "explain" endpoint for admins: why rule X matched (show offsets, feature activations)

Bottom line: favor hybrid approach. Start conservative (flag-only) then iterate to redaction/deny as we gather signals and SecOps buy-in.

-- Priya
(last tinkered 2026-03-05)
